_comment: Template for a new language. Copy it (e.g. to mahara-nl.json) and fill it in. Keys starting with _ are comments and are dropped on load; list entries with "_example": true are dropped too. An almost empty profile is valid: then only the structural checks run, which are already half the value.
_comment_workflow: Where the content comes from: run 'mahara-lang-tool analyze --export EXPORT.po --out analysis.md' first and go through the report. Sections 1 and 2 show which terms are translated inconsistently — those become 'terms' and 'collisions'. Section 4 counts the 'forms' once you have added some. Decide with a native speaker who knows the pack; the report counts, it does not decide.
_comment_plural: Optional: without 'plural_forms' the Plural-Forms line of the export header is used. If you set it, it must have the same nplurals as the export.
_comment_guidelines: Free text, goes verbatim into the brief for the translator: the conventions of this language that a translator has to follow, in plain words, and how to treat placeholders and markup. The more concrete and the more backed by the existing translations, the better.
_comment_glossary: Fixed equivalents. 'source' is searched as a whole word unless a 'pattern' is given. Hits are listed per unit in the scaffold.
_comment_terms: Counted against the existing translations: which variant prevails? The most frequent one is the house form; deviations in new drafts are reported. 'source' searches the English, 'variants' search the translation (regular expressions, case-insensitive). Units whose translation matches no variant are counted as 'none of these' in the analysis. A term is only found where the English still contains it; for a word the source has replaced, use a form. One term per meaning: several source words in one term only if the language uses the same word for them. Add "blocking": true to a term to make a deviation from its house form stop the build (see _comment_blocking).
_comment_collisions: The sharpest check: one target word covering several source terms, swallowing a distinction the source makes. Candidates are in section 2 of the analysis.
_comment_forms: Linguistic forms that are counted in the translations, whatever the English says. "wanted": false reports every hit as a note: use it for whatever makes this language inconsistent. Wanted forms are only counted. The analysis shows sample hits: check them, a pattern that also hits something else gives wrong numbers. Add "blocking": true to an unwanted form to make every hit stop the build (see _comment_blocking).
_comment_blocking: What stops the build until a translation is fixed or its unit has a "note" explaining it. Preferred: "blocking": true on a single term or unwanted form, for rules the person decided and whose sample hits are clean. The list below switches whole kinds of notes instead: term, form, title_material, title_cosmetic, craft, unchanged, sentences. A rule that blocks makes an agent follow it instead of skipping it; a rule with false alarms costs a note each time, so leave such a rule non-blocking rather than delete it.
_comment_placeholders: Only change if the project is not Mahara/PHP. The default covers sprintf (%s, %d, %1$s) and Mahara's {$a->foo}.
_comment_skip: Files whose strings are not prose. In Mahara that is langconfig.php with its date formats: %d and %m there are not placeholders.
_comment_repeated: Words that may legitimately appear twice in a row in this language.
_comment_titles: Removed before comparing a help title with its field label: everything that may differ cosmetically between the two in this language (regular expressions).
_comment_batch: Units per batch. 80 has worked well: small enough to finish in one go, large enough to keep the number of files manageable.
_comment_agent: Additional instructions that go into the brief under the guidelines — working method rather than language rules.
agent_notes: Work through a batch in order and do not skip numbers — 'status' and 'check' report missing ones.
If the source is doubtful, do not guess silently: translate what is there and record the case in a note.
